front.title: Agent Authenticator: Hardware-Bound, Origin-Bound Authentication for AI Agents

abstract.t: This document specifies the Agent Authenticator, a mechanism that lets autonomous software agents, such as AI coding agents, authenticate to services with properties comparable to passkeys: keys held in secure hardware, no shared secrets, binding to the service's origin that a manipulated agent cannot override, attested execution environments, and explicit human approval of each agent and of high- risk actions. The same protocol serves agents on personal computers and in cloud environments. It is a profile over existing mechanisms rather than a new identity system: it uses OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange, the Identity Assertion JSON Web Token (JWT) Authorization Grant, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) authorization, and it binds each agent action to a signed, tamper-evident record.
